# `submissions/`

One `<team>_v<N>.parquet` per submission, each with a `.meta.json` sidecar
written by `submit.py` recording exactly which run produced it.

**The index is [`submissions.csv`](submissions.csv)** — generated by
`build_submission_index.py` from those sidecars, joined to the review tier in
`../pipeline_review.csv` and to the board scores in
[`board_scores.csv`](board_scores.csv). Regenerate it after every new
submission:

```bash
python build_submission_index.py
```

## Board scores live in `board_scores.csv`, not in the index

`submissions.csv` is **generated** — it writes only its own fixed column list,
so anything hand-added to it is deleted on the next run. Board scores used to
be kept there, in hand-added `actual ` / `Date of submission` / `personal
notes` columns, one regeneration away from being lost. They are the only
evidence in this build that cannot be re-derived from anything on disk: they
come from the scorer.

They now live in `board_scores.csv`, which the generator **only ever reads**.
Add a row there after each upload; `build_submission_index.py` joins it in and
warns about any submitted version with no score recorded.

## Current state (2026-09-21)

**Best: v29 = 293.6685** — `airport_operator_multimodel msmlp18fi` (v25) with
the TabNet mix applied to LIRF rows at w = 0.55. v28 is the same recipe at
w = 0.80 (294.4929), v25 the un-overridden base (295.2054).

31 rows in the index: 28 versions plus v18's three cap variants.

### What is and is not rebuildable

`submit.py` takes `--arm` from `config.ARMS`, so an arm that is not in that
list cannot be rebuilt by the current code. Three classes:

| | versions | status |
|---|---|---|
| tier-E arms in `overtuned/` | v4–v12 | **NOT rebuildable, by design.** They are on the leaderboard; the quarantine is the point. |
| built outside `submit.py` | v18 (×3), v28, v29 | v18's caps are hand-built probes and stay that way. **v28/v29's recipe is now registered** as the `tabnet_lirf_override` arm, and their metas point at it via `rebuild_arm`/`rebuild_tag`. Note the rebuild is not byte-identical to the uploaded files -- see "rounding" below. |
| never registered | v26 | **Fixed 2026-09-21.** `airport_operator_catboost_multimodel` had a pipeline, a `predict_ranking()` branch and a `PARENTS` entry but was missing from `config.ARMS`, so the index reported v26 as NOT REBUILDABLE. Added. |

Why this matters concretely: the **Sep 4 data refresh** grew
`submitting.parquet` from 215,876 to 344,841 rows and forced a rebuild of all
17 submissions then in existence — v17's upload was rejected outright
("missing 128,965 required rows"). Anything not rebuildable through
`submit.py` has to be reassembled by hand when that happens.

The `tabnet_lirf_override` arm records a seed list and applies it; it does
**not** retrain TabNet. Its predictions come from
`../tests_tabnet/build/final_seed<N>.npz`, which hold predictions for the
ranking rows that existed when they were written — not model binaries. If
`ranking.parquet` grows, both the arm's `train.py` and `submit.py` fail loudly
on an id-coverage check rather than shipping a partial override, and recovery
means re-running `train_tabnet_pred.py final <seed>` for each recorded seed
(~80 min each, deterministic — the 2025 training data is untouched by a
ranking refresh).

### Rounding: a rebuild of v28/v29 is not byte-identical

`submit.py` writes `np.rint(pred).astype("int32")` -- predictions are rounded to
whole seconds. The ad-hoc `tests_tabnet/build_candidate.py` that produced v28/v29
instead cast with `.astype(int32)`, which **truncates**. So rebuilding through the
registered arm shifts the 26,899 LIRF rows by 0 or 1 second (about +0.5 s on
average); every non-LIRF row is unchanged, and the float arithmetic before the
cast matches the uploaded files exactly.

The arm deliberately keeps `rint`, because that is what every other submission in
this build used and consistency across the pipeline is worth more than matching
one historical file. Practical consequence, stated rather than buried: the board's
**293.6685 belongs to the truncated file**, and a rebuilt v29 is a hair different
from the artifact that scored it.

## Known gaps in the record

- **v27's meta** records `feature_fingerprint: null` for its `per_airport` and
  `per_operator` provenance entries while `airport_operator_blend` records
  `aeade7fee3099c1a`. The fingerprint gate is the build's main anti-staleness
  control; a null there is an unverified link, not a verified one.
- **v18's three sidecars were written retroactively** (2026-09-21) from the
  parquets and the plan-13 record — they carry
  `meta_written_retroactively` saying so. Only `cap7200` was uploaded.
- Nine submissions (v4–v12) **skipped the full-period refit**, training on the
  `forward` split's 8 months (1,387,105 rows) when `full`'s 12 months
  (2,084,659) were available. The build's design is *select on `forward`,
  refit on `full`, submit*; `full` is in `config.SELECTION_FORBIDDEN_SPLITS`
  precisely so nothing can be chosen on it.

## Renamed 2026-09-08: `PLACEHOLDER_TEAM_*` → `fearless_barn_*`

`submit.py --team` was a required free-text argument with no default, so every
submission up to v13 was typed by hand as `PLACEHOLDER_TEAM` and 12 files were
built under that placeholder name. The competition contract keys the file on the
registered team name (`<team>_v<N>.parquet`), so this was not cosmetic.

All 13 files were renamed and the `team` field inside each `.meta.json` updated.
The team name now lives in `config.TEAM` and `submit.py --team` defaults to it,
so it cannot be mistyped again.

**Plan documents in `../plans/` (05–13) still reference the old
`PLACEHOLDER_TEAM_v*.parquet` paths.** Those are historical records of past
rounds and have deliberately not been rewritten — the links are stale, the
filenames map one-to-one by version number.

> If any of v1–v12 were actually uploaded under the placeholder name, the
> leaderboard's copy still carries that name; only the local files changed.

## Uploading

`submit.py` never uploads. It prints the `mc` command and leaves sending a file
as an explicit human action, so a half-finished model cannot burn a submission
slot by accident. Credentials live in `../../credentials.json` (git-ignored).
The board requires the hyphen form `fearless-barn_vN.parquet`; local files use
the underscore form. Limit: 5 submissions/day, and ranking takes the **best**
RMSE across all of them, so a diagnostic probe cannot hurt your standing.
